title: When Lester left and whether he returned
summary: They sort out dates for Lester's leaving, the Kansas City Five records and his Army service.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But, can you see where Lester comes back?
No, I can't. And, yet I thought he did come back.
I thought Lester did come back. For a time.
I don't remember whether he came back -- now what year is that? That's '46 you say that Lester never did -- well when did he leave -- Lester left?
And, when did Don Byas and --
They went in in '42. Don Byas went in in '42 -- Lester must have left before that, didn't he? Let me see -- the last one with Lester. Lester is here in 1940 and then he's gone.
Wait a second. No, he's gone before -- when he went -- that's when they got Paul Bascomb.
Oh yeah? Oh, yeah. It was probably a quick thing --
-- and they had to get somebody right away.
And, then right after that Don came in.
Right. Right. That's what happened. That's why Paul was there. Because Lester left -- it was a quick thing. But, as far as Lester coming back --
Now, Lester is here on a broadcast in 1943. But, I would think he's just a guest or something.
Now then, he plays on those Kansas City Five records.
He plays on those Kansas City Five records, which you made for Harry Lim.
Is that the one that I song on?
Yeah, Lester --. Lester Leaps In, Destination, K.C.,
Wait a minute -- wait a minute -- Destination and what?

This is the small -- it says Buck, Dicky, Lester, Basie, Rodney Richardson on bass, and Jo Jones. Yeah, well, Lester for some reason or other was out, you know, in the early '40's and then he comes back for a time before he goes in the Army.
That doesn't make sense, does it, Freddie?
I'm not disputing that, because I really don't remember.
Well, he must have gone in the Army about '44.
When did the Americans -- when did the U.S. get in the war?
No. Later than that I think.
-- towards the end of '44 -- that's when Lucky Thompson came in --
So, he was out, and then he came back. So, what he was out for I don't know.
No I think it was '41 -- December 7, 1941. I think. That the Americans went into the war.
Yeah, but he wouldn't go in the Army -- he wouldn't go into the Army then.
But, basically, all these tenors are replacing Lester.
You know -- he's got one after another.
I don't have no idea why he left.
I mean, I don't even -- Lester wasn't in very long either, was he -- because I think he was inslided out,
I'm just wondering if he -- when he got out -- when he got out of the Army -- whether he stayed, or whether he went to California or what happened.
Well, he joined up with Lee for awhile, do you remember? He was in a little band with his brother -- with Lee.
Well, this isn't really, you know, this isn't really very important. I mean, these facts are well known. I mean, you're not getting any --
No, but all we wanted to find out was did he ever get back with the band again after he got out of the Army. That's the only thing we were asking about that.
